line: Framework Laptop 16 (2025, AMD Ryzen AI 300 Series, DIY Edition)
config_name: Laptop 16 DIY — Ryzen AI 7 350, 32GB DDR5 (2x16GB), 1TB NVMe, Expansion Bay shell (no dGPU)

specs.cpu: AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 (8-core/16-thread Zen 5/5c, up to 5.0GHz)
specs.gpu: Radeon 860M integrated (RDNA 3.5); Expansion Bay empty (dGPU module optional later)
specs.ports: 6x user-swappable Expansion Card slots (USB-C/USB-A/HDMI/DP/Ethernet/microSD/storage; cards sold separately) + Expansion Bay (shell fitted), 3.5mm
specs.keyboard_notes: Full-size backlit with numpad option; replaceable assembly
specs.os: None (DIY — bring your own; Windows or Linux)

battery.notes: 85Wh. Users report ~7-9h light use without dGPU; 165Hz panel costs some runtime.

price.notes: Configurator component sum (2026-11-24): AI 7 350 base $2,178 + 32GB +$750 (assumed same as FW13) + 1TB +$300. Excludes 6 expansion cards + OS. Sold via pre-order batches (most sold out; Batch 9 ships Dec) — fulfillment delay is a real caveat.

reviews.quote: first laptop ever to earn a 10/10 repairability score

praises: Only mainstream laptop where the GPU is a swappable module — buy the shell now, add a dGPU years later
Expansion Bay shell keeps it thin and light; configurator calls it "The default thin and light end cap for the Expansion Bay interface that includes system cooling"
Six expansion-card slots — more port variety than any 16-inch ultrabook
Socketed RAM, dual M.2 slots, and every module sold as a documented self-service spare
165Hz matte 16-inch panel is smooth and glare-free; big speakers for the class
complaints: Pre-order batch system: nearly all batches sold out, shipping slips to December/Q1 — top FW16 complaint
2.1kg and thick bezels make it the least portable 16-inch ultrabook
Six expansion cards (~$15-36 each) are required for a complete machine but cost extra
Without the dGPU module, gaming is just an iGPU in a big chassis
No numeric pro review coverage of the AI 300 FW16 tier found this pass

design_philosophy: Framework Laptop 16 extends the modular platform to the desktop-replacement class: a hot-upgradeable Expansion Bay for swappable dGPU modules, six user-chosen ports, and full self-service internals. The shell (no-dGPU) config is the price- and weight-conscious entry — the bay means discrete graphics is a future purchase, not a today tax.
standouts: Expansion Bay means discrete GPU is a future slide-in purchase, not a today tax
6 expansion-card slots + dual M.2 + socketed RAM: most modular 16-inch on the market
dealbreakers: Pre-order batch system — most batches sold out, shipping December/Q1
